avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 induction; reduces nortriptyline levels and efficacy; increases serotonin syndrome risk
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; discontinue at least 2 weeks before starting nortriptyline

avoid_supplements.name: SAMe (S-Adenosyl Methionine)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive serotonergic effects; increases risk of serotonin syndrome
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; monitor for agitation, tremor, hyperthermia

avoid_supplements.name: Tramadol-containing supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Serotonin syndrome risk; both increase serotonergic activity

caution_supplements.name: 5-HTP
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms (tremor, agitation, confusion)

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential stimulant effects may potentiate anticholinergic side effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased cardiovascular effects or dry mouth

caution_supplements.name: Valerian Root
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased sedation or dizziness

avoid_foods.name: Tyramine-rich foods (aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented products)
avoid_foods.mechanism: TCAs inhibit monoamine oxidase; excessive tyramine can cause hypertensive crisis
avoid_foods.action: Counsel on moderation; excessive intake may elevate blood pressure

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase nortriptyline levels
caution_foods.action: Limit consumption; monitor for increased anticholinergic effects

caution_foods.name: Caffeine
caution_foods.action: Moderate intake; monitor for tremor, palpitations, or insomnia

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS depression and anticholinergic effects
caution_foods.action: Minimize alcohol consumption; counsel on impaired cognition and sedation risk

monitoring_notes: Nortriptyline undergoes significant hepatic metabolism via CYP2D6; monitor for anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation) and serotonin syndrome when combined with other serotonergic agents. Baseline and periodic ECG monitoring is recommended due to cardiac effects.
